rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (kp 2.0, search_right, base_speed 1.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, sensors at x = ±0.04 and ±0.015/0) is the best raced design, at 75.779. Compared with iteration 4 (kp 2.5), progress rose on every track: oval 0.21 to 0.29, s-bend 0.126 to 0.153, slalom 0.084 to 0.108. Every run still ended off track with one line-loss event, and max_error stayed at about 0.063 to 0.067 m, above the 0.06 m limit. Oscillation stayed low (0.14 to 0.16), so the robot is drifting to an edge, not weaving. Changing kp is the only change that has moved progress in the right direction, and the trend is monotonic across the 2.5 to 2.0 step. The Evaluator's branch 1 (max_error below 0.06 m) is not met, but progress did rise on all three tracks, so turn authority is still a limiter.

Change. I keep the iteration 5 geometry, base_speed 1.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, sensor weights and search_right, and lower kp from 2.0 to 1.6, the lower part of the 1.5 to 1.8 range the Evaluator named. This is a single-variable continuation of the kp trend. Choosing 1.6 rather than 1.5 keeps a margin against losing the line on bend entries.

Expected result. Progress should rise again on the oval, s-bend and slalom, with a score above 75.8. max_error may stay near 0.063 m because the failure point seems to lie beyond proportional authority. Fallback: if progress falls or line-loss events rise, revert to kp 2.0, the best raced design, and move to the sensor-geometry test (sensor_size 0.016 at the same x positions).

Hypotheses. H7: lower kp reduces bend-entry overshoot, so the robot keeps more progress before reaching the edge. H8: max_error stays near 0.063 m, so the edge exit is caused by something other than proportional gain. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error and line_loss_events per track, and whether the loss point moves along the course.
